notes: IOPS port. Faithful variant always takes +y (mirrors far-side anchors); disambiguated resolves the y-sign against an already-placed off-axis anchor (literature-standard closed form). Baseline the grid/PF methods were originally seeded from.

classical = Torgerson/Gower double centering on the shortest-path-completed matrix (MDS-MAP recipe of Shang et al. 2003); smacof_* = de Leeuw stress majorization (Guttman transform); robust variants multiply stress weights by the shared kernel weights per IRLS iteration. Also the shared init family: classical MDS on the session-median matrix of the view over all epochs for factor_graph and on the median ranges of the first 20 epochs for ekf and particle_filter, and the bipartite init of the SLAM estimators.
One range factor per observed anchor pair; kernel realized as IRLS weights inside the LM loop; gauge fixed by parameterization (anchor 0 origin, anchor 1 on +x).

M-estimation Kalman filtering via IRLS-style R inflation (R_eff = sigma^2/w, one IRLS step per scalar update); gated variant = innovation gating at NIS 9 (3-sigma chi-square, 1 dof). Zero process noise (static anchors); state dim 2n-3 (gauge removed).

estimator_class: sequential Monte Carlo (per-anchor conditional bootstrap PF)
notes: Joint 2n-dim PF intractable; per-anchor particle sets conditioned on posterior means of the others (Gauss-Seidel). Per-node beliefs as in nonparametric BP and SPAWN, but conditioned on point estimates and without messages (paper Sec. V-D). Two sweeps with re-scatter; seeded method.

Faithful port of the IOPS histogram + probability-grid pipeline (own PGP grid prior work); Bucy 1971 = point-mass filter origin. mixture variant keeps the original mechanism peculiarity: likelihoods SUMMED over reference anchors instead of multiplied.

Causal filter over [mobile pose | anchors] with zero anchor process noise; robust R-inflation kernel axis as ekf. The filter commits to the basin of its bipartite-MDS start, and the robust weights can suppress the updates that would repair a bad start, which may explain its lock-in on set_b/s01; on s02 it ends below the batch solver (paper Sec. V-C, VI-D).

estimator_class: batch robust NLS (pose-chain factor graph; sparse LM)
notes: Pose chain + anchors jointly (arrowhead sparsity, scipy.sparse normal equations); Gaussian motion factors, kernel axis on range factors only. Re-linearizes over 15 to 36 LM iterations and recovers from inits where the causal EKF-SLAM cannot - a family finding.

estimator_class: cross-cutting: robust loss kernels (IRLS weights / pseudo-likelihoods)
notes: Shared dimensionless rho(u), u = r/sigma; constants fixed a-priori at the 95% Gaussian-efficiency values of the M-estimation literature (Huber 1964, Zhang 1997): Huber k = 1.345, Cauchy c = 2.385. Nothing tuned against the evaluation metric; makes the result tables factorial in estimator class x kernel.

Least-squares rigid transform (rotation and translation, no scale) between estimate and ground truth with reflection allowed; every reference implementation is evaluated after alignment (solution frames are gauge-free or convention-gauged).

estimator_class: cross-cutting: topology views of one measurement graph (paper Sec. IV-C)
notes: Companion review + corpus exemplars anchoring the four mask families; one dataset, controlled edge-masking as the connectivity/information axis. Static suite runs on fully_meshed/multi_hop/mobile_assisted; ekf_slam only on slam_bipartite (no anchor-anchor pairs there), and fg_slam also on the mobile-assisted view of the set_b walks.

Internal doctrine, no external cite: sigma = max(median per-pair epoch scatter, 1.4826*MAD of classical-MDS init residuals), computed ONCE per session from its fully_meshed view and shared by every mask of that session (sigma measures hardware + environment, not topology). Values: set_b/s03 0.129 m, set_a/s21 1.621 m.
